item.title: Federal Reserve Confirms It Has Considered Acting, And That Consideration, It Turns Out, Is The Entire Job
item.description: Officials confirmed that the committee had considered acting several times this quarter and that, for a central bank, considering is not a step toward acting but the whole of the work. Acting, they clarified, is what other countries do, and is widely felt here to be a rumor.

item.title: Fund Prospectus Clarifies That Its Risk Disclosure Is A Genre, Not A Warning
item.description: The fund, responding to confusion among holders, confirmed that the lengthy passage headed Principal Risks is prepared in the literary tradition of the risk disclosure, a form, and is not intended to represent actual risks, which are enumerated, the fund says, nowhere.

item.title: Fully Passive ETF Announces It Will Own Nothing, Because That Is The Most Passive Position Anyone Has Taken
item.description: The fund, which will hold no securities, no cash and no cargo of any kind, confirmed its benchmark is the score the market would have received had it declined to answer, a figure the fund computes daily and declines to show. Officials called the approach not investing but posture, and confirmed the office.

item.title: Company Decides To Ask And Answer Its Own Questions This Quarter, Confirms The Questions Were Always The Best Part
item.description: The company, citing a Q&A that had, in its words, gone poorly, has elected to both pose and answer the analyst questions in-house, a format it described as fairer. Analysts, listening to the firm interview itself, praised the answers as remarkably on-message and, frankly, unimprovable.

item.title: Family Office Hires A Family, Because Finding Real Ones Willing To Share A Balance Sheet Has Taken Longer Than Expected
item.description: The office, its founding family having declined one by one to attend, has retained a professional family to sit at the head of its quarterly table, confirming the new members love the assets like their own and have signed nothing to mean it. The founding family, reached, said it was having a nice summer.

item.title: Tape Rallies On The Report Of A Moth At The Podium, Market Confirms It Was, Technically, A Market Event
item.description: The composite advanced after a moth, entering the floor briefly and exiting to applause, was read by the desk as confirmation the tape had not yet peaked. A floor official, standing where the moth had stood, confirmed the rally was textbook and that the moth had declined to comment.

item.title: Streaming Service Launches A New Tier That, For More Money, Lets You Scheme To Leave, Which Is The Only Tier Anyone Uses
item.description: The service, having noticed that its most popular plan was the one people used to plot their departure, has formalized it as a premium tier: ExitMax, for a modest increase, lets subscribers watch the platform, watch competitors, and watch a countdown of their own cancellation, which the platform confirmed is the feature with, by far, the highest renewal surprise.

item.title: The Federal Reserve Retires The Word Zero, And Rates, Freed From The Number, Are Now Whatever They Need To Be
item.description: At a brief ceremony this morning, the central bank struck the concept of zero from its internal vocabulary, explaining that a rate of zero had become, frankly, embarrassing, and that rates would henceforth be expressed in more uplifting terms, beginning at some. The word one, officials said, is not yet ready, but one is optimistic.

item.title: Inflation Gauge Retires After It Kept Making Families Feel Poor, Bureau Cites Emotional Toll On The Data
item.description: The Bureau announced it will cease publishing its headline price index, explaining that the number, while technically accurate, had developed a habit of arriving at a bad time and making whole households feel bad about themselves. Officials said the series declined to comment further, citing the toll.

item.title: The IPO Roadshow Has Become A Catered Ceremony Where The Company Is There In Spirit And The Investors Are There For The Sandwich
item.description: The banker confirmed the roadshow's real deliverable was never the story, which was on a slide, but the room, which featured a sandwich. The company's CEO, present for the opening toast, departed for a call and did not return, a schedule that multiple investors, plate in hand, described as the strongest signal of the entire offering.

item.title: Regulator Approves A Rule Whose Fine Print Is Readable Only From A Second Address You Do Not Own
item.description: After an extended review, the regulator has certified the new disclosure regime as fully compliant, a determination reached in part because the operative paragraph, visible only from the property line of a mailing address currently in escrow, was deemed by review staff to be technically not there, and therefore impossible to violate.

item.title: Law Firm Unveils A Trust For Clients Who Have Nobody To Leave It To, Confirms The Nobody Is Taxed Separately
item.description: The firm, addressing a growing demographic, has introduced the Legacy of Last Resort, a trust for clients whose heirs are, in the firm's delicate phrasing, administratively unavailable. The trust will hold the client's assets in perpetuity, forever, which the firm confirmed is longer than any family, and therefore, statistically, the safest mailbox the money will ever know.
